idiom_name: module of functions over SQLAlchemy Core Table/Row (or pandas frames)
implementation_notes: Python's Table Module is a module, not a class: functions per table take a Connection and return Row objects from select(table) or plain dicts/dataclasses - the result list is the record set. SQLAlchemy Core supplies the table-level primitives (Table, select/update/insert with .where(), Row) while the business rules stay ordinary functions, which is why the class-per-table structure disappears; pandas is the same idea for in-memory record sets. Write a class only when the module needs configuration, such as a gateway or schema object, and never build one object per row.
pitfalls: A Connection is inside a transaction from its first statement: without an explicit conn.commit() (SQLAlchemy 2.0 begin-once semantics) the module's writes are rolled back at close, which looks like a lost update.
Row objects are tuple-like with attribute access, so code that expects dicts breaks on .get()/.keys(); pick one row shape per module and keep module-level caches from holding rows across sessions.
